newsitem.title: CHINA: China tells Japan not to provoke islands incidents.
newsitem.headline: China tells Japan not to provoke islands incidents.

text.p: China on Tuesday urged Japan not to provoke new trouble in a row over disputed islands in the East China Sea, one day after Tokyo repelled a flotilla of Hong Kong and Taiwanese protest ships from the chain.
"We hope the Japanese government could adopt truly effective measures and not provoke new incidents," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesman Shen Guofang told a news briefing.

Hong Kong and Taiwan organisers of a high seas challenge to Tokyo's claim over the islands, called the Diaoyus in Chinese and the Senkakus in Japanese, returned on Tuesday after Japanese coastguard vessels stopped them from landing on the group.
Spokesman Shen sidestepped a question on whether China stood ready to support any attempt by individuals who fell overboard from the protest boats to seek compensation from Tokyo.
He reiterated Beijing's stance that the Diaoyus were Chinese territory and blamed Tokyo for raising tensions by allowing Japanese rightist groups to land on the potentially resource-rich archipelago.
"The responsibility lies totally with the Japanese side," Shen said, adding that Japan should prevent further landings on the group by rightist activists.
"Concerning the actions by Japan that have infringed on China's territorial sovereignty many times, we have repeatedly made diplomatic representations to the Japanese government," Shen said.
Tensions flared anew earlier this month when a conservative Japanese legislator and three other Japanese landed on one of the islands to plant a flag and hold a memorial ceremony.
In response, ethnic Chinese activists aboard some 20 Taiwan and Hong Kong vessels sailed to the disputed chain on Monday and tried to land on one of the islets to assert China's claims.
Japan sent 60 coastguard vessels -- some armed -- and used their superior numbers to keep the protest boats at bay.
Protest organisers called off their landing attempts after several minor collisions, one of which sent several journalists overboard. All were quickly rescued.

Rival claims to the islands by China, Japan and Taiwan have stirred nationalist passion in Chinese communities in Hong Kong, Taiwan and North America since a Japanese rightist group built a makeshift lighthouse there in July 1996.
